title: Approximation by a Sparse Fourier Hypothesis
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of the $n$ coordinates, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq\frac12$. Suppose the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ outside $\mathcal{F}$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$. Suppose also that each rational coefficient assigned to a set in $\mathcal{F}$ differs from the corresponding Fourier coefficient of $f$ by at most $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal{F}|)$. The Boolean function obtained by taking the sign of the resulting sparse Fourier sum, with nonnegative values assigned sign $+1$, has relative Hamming distance at most $\varepsilon$ from $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$\mathcal{F}$ is a nonempty finite family of coordinate subsets
Fourier weight outside $\mathcal{F}$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$
Each assigned rational coefficient has error at most $\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal{F}|)$
